Head Coach Kyle Shanahan Press Conference

Head Coach Kyle Shanahan

Press Conference – November 25, 2026

San Francisco 49ers

Listen to Audio I Media Center

Opening comments:

“Injuries for practice today. [DB] Siran Neal won’t practice, knee/foot. [LB Dre] Greenlaw won’t practice, neck. [WR] Mike Evans won’t practice, Achilles. [WR Jordan] Watkins won’t practice, groin. [QB] Brock Purdy won’t practice, ankle. [OL] Carver Willis, limited, illness. [DB Deommodore Lenoir] DMo, limited, foot. [CB Upton] Stout, limited, shoulder/neck. [OL Austen] Pleasants, limited, knee. Go ahead.”

When did Brock get injured?

“Second quarter.”

Any concern behind the ankle with him or you think he’ll probably be able to get out there later this week?

“We’ll see. Concern today, couldn’t go.”

How’s Dre progressing?

“I think he’s doing good. He usually gets Wednesdays off anyways, but I know he still feels his neck, so we’ll see how he is tomorrow.”

Were you aware that Brock got injured in the second quarter?

“Yeah, I was.”

Did that affect your play calling or anything?

“No, nothing. They always tell you when someone has something, but then they come back and they’re like, ‘Hey, checked out, he should be fine.’ He didn’t miss any plays or anything.”

You’re not going to have OL Colton McKivitz the rest of the way. Do you feel like he was playing at a Pro Bowl-caliber level before he got hurt?

“Yeah, I do. I thought he was playing really well. I thought he played close to that last year and I think he’s only gotten better this year. I was really hurt for him that he couldn’t finish this year because he’s had a hell of a year.”

Is there a concern that Brock’s injury could threaten his availability for Sunday?

“I mean, he can’t go today, so it’s always a possibility. It’s not a high ankle so it’s day-to-day with it, but we’ve got to see how it goes.”

You faced an elite defense last week. You’re facing another elite defense this week. In what ways are they similar and in what ways are they different?

“They’re similar in they both have really good numbers, but two totally different styles of defense. Minnesota, it’s just those blitzes. There’s a threat of it every single play and these guys are a heavy two-shell defense. They mix in blitzes throughout the game like everybody does, but definitely not as many blitzes.”

Would you say OL Verderian Lowe will be the starting right tackle moving forward?

“Yes.”

How did he play on Sunday night filling in and obviously you brought him here for a reason, what’s your assessment of what he was and how he’s been since he’s been here?

“I thought he played real well. Coming in, especially going against that defense, just all the problems that they present, so I thought he came in and stepped it up really well. That’s why we brought him here. Anytime you have a swing tackle, that means you better be capable of starting. He’s started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter and that’s why we targeted him as a swing tackle.”

How big of a luxury was it to have the same starting five offensive linemen through 10 games and how much better did they get because of that consistency?

“It’s huge. Just the more you play with an O-Line, the more you play as 11 guys together on offense, the better you get just moving together and nothing’s more important than the O-Line in that area. We had been very fortunate, had our first big loss. Vederian’s got a lot of reps though. He always takes [T] Trent’s [Williams] reps on Wednesday and then we rotate him at the other positions on the other days, so he’s ready to take over.”

There aren’t a ton of running backs that have aged as gracefully as RB Christian McCaffrey has in terms of his production. I know you’ve talked about his professionalism and his work ethic and all those things, but is there any part of you that’s surprised or what do you think is the key that’s allowed him to play at this level at that position at this age?

“One, he takes care of himself and prepares like no other. That’s why we call him a psycho because it’s not normal. Everything he does, he’s preparing to play, whether it’s how he sleeps, how he walks down the hallway, everything. So, it’s amazing in that way. I also think it’s a lot with all of our guys who have gotten older, who are Hall of Fame players, that some guys are like that because they’re just so talented and different than everybody. You can’t be a Hall of Fame player if you aren’t like that, but our group of guys, they’re also really special in just their awareness and how they play the game. From both of our wideouts, to our tight end, to our linebacker, to our rusher. They’re very smart players and the game comes very natural to them. Even if you aren’t exactly the same as you were at 23, they still have a lot of other special qualities about them.”

With Mike and the Achilles tendonitis, it’s a load management injury. Will you the rest of the year manage him differently than you had before in terms of not practicing on Wednesdays?

“I think to a degree. I mean, we were doing that from the beginning anyways. I think Mike’s done that for the last few years of his career, so you’ve got to manage him that way anyways. He probably would never practice Wednesdays regardless, but yeah, the Achilles. He took four or five weeks off, whatever it was and then we tried to be smart with him through the game, just not to up his wear and tear too much. That’s why we don’t want to leave him out there all the time and that’ll continue. The Achilles can get better as the year goes and we can forget about that, but it still probably won’t change as far as Wednesdays and things like that.”

Where is Pleasants in his rehab and is he a possibility to be activated?

“Yeah, he is a possibility. He’s been healthy for a few weeks now. With losing Colton, it makes sense to get him out practicing and we’ll see how this week goes, but he’s been healthy for a bit. We’ll see how his practices go, see if he’s ready to go and if he is we’ll make a decision.”

Christian gave some insight on what it’s like to have to deal with Achilles tendonitis a couple of weeks ago. About how nagging it can be and how hard it can be to just get up and get out of the bed. If there was any conversation between you and Mike Evans, how did he express to you that he felt good enough to go and how he’s been feeling as he continues to kind of progress with this?

“We don’t overtalk those things. I listen to the doctors and he tells me he’s ready to go and then I watch him and decide on what I see based off of what they tell me. There’s not a lot of discussions. We don’t overdo that.”

There was a lot of joking around in the locker room about how WR Keenan Allen and Mike Evans are the uncles of the room. How has it been game planning with them, seeing them work together on the field?

“It’s awesome. Kind of what I was just saying with Christian. They’re still unbelievably talented, but just the intelligence of both of them and just the poise they have and how competitive they are and how good they are at whatever you ask them to do. Just how good of blockers they are, how good they are at routes that you haven’t seen them run before. It’s whatever you put in, they figure out. As you see, it’s exactly what I was saying about Christian. They’re both generational talents, but the reason they’re doing it at such a high level is because they have that talent but there’s also, I feel like, their generational awareness and how good of football players they are also.”

Have you enjoyed game planning with both of those two guys in mind?

“Yeah, big time because they’ve got certain attributes that are awesome for a quarterback with both of their hands and their size and then just how easy things come to them with. They don’t seem overwhelmed with what we put in.”

When the game ends, how quickly do you start the next week’s game plan? How long does it take you to finish it?

“It takes me a while to finish the game from Sunday. I do it on my own all Sunday night. Then I do it with the offensive coaches to start. Then I do it with the defensive coaches second. Then I talk to the special teams coaches. Then I meet with the team. Then I meet with the quarterbacks. Then I do a press conference. Then I’ll usually talk to [principal owner] Jed [York]. Then it’s like four o’clock and I’ll have lunch and start the next game. That’s why it’s awesome when we give them days off and you guys don’t make me have a press conference on Mondays. Then we start around Monday at four o’clock. At least I do. Everyone else starts when they’re done with me on Monday morning, and then we don’t stop until kickoff.”

You’ve been on the road for two weeks and they’ve got a seven-day rest advantage on you. Are there things that you can do this time of year to take foot off the gas pedal or ease up or do things to freshen up your team before Sunday?

“Yeah, you have to do both. It’s a fine line either way. You’ve got to understand the reality of that. Just similar to how it was last year, we didn’t get a Bye until December, so things like that you’ve always got to take into account. Traveling is different and then always facing a team coming off a Bye week is different. You’re looking at Wednesday’s practice, things like that, We’ll slow it down a little bit more today, just like we did last week, but then you do too much and half your team’s not ready to play and half it helped. So, it’s a very fine line and you’ve got to try to balance it out.”

Mike was singularly great for you against Seattle. Now that you have Keenan, does that give you an advantage to attack their two-shell defense?

“The more players you have out there, obviously always the better. Mike had an unbelievable game versus them last time, but I thought a lot of other guys stepped up too. But, just having another guy out there makes your percentages a lot higher of making the right plays because there’s no plays off with these guys. They never give you an easy one. Every coverage is tight. There’s the least amount of space you’ll ever see in the NFL. They’re as good as it gets.”

Asking just because a neck injury sounds like it’s a little different. Is there any concern with Greenlaw that that’s a long-term issue?

“I don’t think so. I think it’s more nerve stuff, which come and go. He felt there was a couple of days where it was getting really good last week and it felt better. Then he woke up one day and it was a lot worse and then that was closer by game time. It’s just a little on-and-off with that stuff, but I felt pretty good about him last week and feel better about him this week so we’ll see how it goes.”

They said on the broadcast you called it the “unc package” with Evans and Keenan. Are you actually calling it that and is it limited to just those two or all the 30-plus guys?

“I don’t really have to because they’re out there for the most part anyways, just being starting receivers and everything. But, we mix in so many guys and I know everybody’s name, but when I’m thinking about football I don’t always just spit out names fast so sometimes it’s just easier for me to say unc. Everyone knows who I’m talking about.”

It’s just those two?

“Yeah.”

How do they like it? Are they okay with it?

“I don’t know. I hope they like it. I think it’s cool. They’re not like really uncles. They’re in their 30s, they’re still young.”

You came up with that?

“I don’t think so. I think everyone did. It think it was just natural. It was obvious.”

Where’s WR De’Zhaun Stribling at? I know you said a December target range. Does he have a chance to get back in practice soon?

“I don’t know. I haven’t asked. I mean, nothing’s changed, so I think it’s a couple weeks away.”

I know you called Christian a psycho. It’s probably endearing to a certain extent.

“Very endearing.”

When you have a guy like that who has been so hard to take off the field, how has he approached the injection of RB Kaelon Black into that role, the complementary role that he’s had, and were there any conversations at any point with Christian about that kind of stuff?

“I always tell him that’s what I’m trying to do. Christian’s very smart, so he understands what’s good about that. He’s also a dog and a competitor and tells me I should never have to worry about anybody else because he can handle anything, which he’s not wrong, but he also knows the benefits of it too. I don’t know if he always likes it, but it’s not something he’s complaining about because he knows it can help him. He also respects Kaelon. When someone goes in there and runs like he does, I think that makes him feel better too.”

You guys officially parted ways with WR Brandon Aiyuk and he’s now joined the Washington Commanders reportedly today. What are your thoughts on him going there?

“None. It was just a transactional thing and it’s good for Washington. They got a good player.”

Why do you guys have a roof on your practice field?

“Because I keep getting told about El Niño or something. We’re expecting it to rain on Sunday, so we’ll practice in the rain, but sometimes when it’s just like a monsoon out there and we’re playing in a bubble, you can get a little bit more done with not being in that. So if it ends up being like that, like people have warned, at least we can walk through and stuff like that. It’s not the tallest thing, so we can’t make all the throws in there, but it just gives us an option, which we haven’t had before if things get bad.”

As far as president of football operations and general manager John Lynch signing an extension, obviously it’s probably not news to you that was going to happen, but I think for some of us it was like, “Well, he’s not quite on your timeline.” Does this suggest that you guys are on a similar timeline and you’re going to finish this thing together?

“Yeah, I always believed that. Timelines just have to do with when guys have agreed to stuff. I’ve done mine earlier than his, but I’ve always seen myself being here only with John and I think he feels the same.”
